:::{#def-differentiable}
#### Differentiable function

A function $f$ is **differentiable at** $x = c$ if the limit

$$f'(c) \eqdef \lim_{h \to 0} \frac{f(c + h) - f(c)}{h}$$

exists and is finite.

[@larsonCalc11e, Section 2.1, p. 100]

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#def-differentiable-on}
#### Differentiable on an interval

A function $f$ is **differentiable on** an interval
if it is differentiable (@def-differentiable) at every interior point of the interval;
at a closed endpoint, the appropriate one-sided derivative is used.

[@larsonCalc11e, Section 2.1, p. 100]

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#def-continuous}
#### Continuous function

A function $f$ is **continuous at** $x = c$ if all three conditions hold:

1. $f(c)$ is defined,
2. $\lim_{x \to c} f(x)$ exists, and
3. $\lim_{x \to c} f(x) = f(c)$.

[@larsonCalc11e, Section 1.4, p. 73]

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#def-continuous-on}
#### Continuous on a closed interval

A function $f$ is **continuous on** a closed interval $[a, b]$
if it is continuous (@def-continuous) at every point of $[a, b]$.

[@larsonCalc11e, Section 1.4, p. 73]

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#def-riemann-integral}
#### Riemann integral

For a bounded function $f$ on $[a, b]$,
split $[a, b]$ into $n$ equal-width subintervals of width
$\Delta x \eqdef (b - a)/n$,
and let $x_i^*$ be any point in the $i$-th subinterval.
The **Riemann integral** of $f$ over $[a, b]$ is the limit

$$\int_a^b f(x)\,dx \eqdef \lim_{n \to \infty} \sum_{i=1}^n f(x_i^*)\,\Delta x,$$

when that limit exists.

[@larsonCalc11e, Section 4.3, p. 272]

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#def-integrable}
#### Riemann integrable

A bounded function $f$ is **Riemann integrable on** $[a, b]$
if its Riemann integral (@def-riemann-integral) over $[a, b]$
exists and is finite.

[@larsonCalc11e, Section 4.3, p. 272]

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#def-integrable-general}
#### General Riemann integrability

More generally, using partitions $\mathcal{P}$ of arbitrary mesh --- subintervals of varying widths
$\Delta x_i$ --- a bounded function $f$ is **Riemann integrable in the general sense** on $[a, b]$ if

$$\int_a^b f(x)\,dx \eqdef \lim_{\|\mathcal{P}\| \to 0} \sum_{i=1}^n f(x_i^*)\,\Delta x_i$$

exists and is finite, where $\|\mathcal{P}\| = \max_i \Delta x_i$ is the mesh of the partition.

:::

:::{#thm-riemann-general}
#### Equivalence of Riemann sum formulations

For continuous $f$ on a closed interval $[a, b]$, the equal-width Riemann sum
(@def-integrable) and the arbitrary-mesh Riemann sum (@def-integrable-general)
give the same value [@rudin1976principles, Chapter 6].
Applied statistics courses mostly use the equal-width form in @def-integrable.

:::
